---
title: "How it works"
---

The polyfill ports phit's Rust code to PHP. It does not reimplement the
methods independently. Each port keeps the extension's algorithm, constants,
branch order, and floating-point operation order, so the two return the same
bits.

## Least squares

`fit_ols` scales the design columns to unit norm and factors the design by
Householder QR, with the operation order of the extension's linear-algebra
library (nalgebra). The singular values of the small $R$ factor, computed by
a Jacobi sweep, equal the design's. The extension's rank rule,
$s \le \varepsilon \cdot \max(n, p) \cdot s_{\max}$, therefore makes the same
rank decisions. Coefficients and covariances come from $R$ by
back-substitution. Weighted fits factor rows in decreasing-weight order, as
the extension does.

## Generalized linear models

`fit_logistic` and `fit_poisson` use damped Newton IRLS, and `fit_probit` uses
Fisher scoring. Each iteration solves a weighted least-squares step with the
same QR, halves the step until the likelihood does not decrease, and stops
only after a small full step. The separation certificate, boundary handling,
starting values for extreme offsets, and exception codes match the extension.

## Mixed models

`fit_mixed_intercept` profiles the variance ratio as the extension does.
`fit_mixed` and `fit_lmer` port the extension's general linear mixed model,
including its BOBYQA and Nelder–Mead optimizers. `fit_logistic_mixed` and
`fit_glmer` port the likelihood (the Laplace approximation, or adaptive
Gauss–Hermite quadrature with 2 to 61 points) and the BOBYQA search.
The optimizers are ported from the same crate versions, so they take the same
steps.

## Distributions

The extension's distribution layer is ported together with the parts of
cdflib that it calls. These are TOMS 708 (incomplete beta), TOMS 654
(incomplete gamma), Cody's normal CDF, and the `dinvnr`/`dt1` quantile starts.
Log-scale tails, Loader's saddle-point densities, and the safeguarded quantile
search are ported as well. The statrs routines that the estimators call (erfc,
$\ln \Gamma$, the regularized incomplete beta, and the inverse error
function) are ported from the same crate version.

## Rounding and fused multiply-add

PHP has no fused multiply-add. The extension's matrix products on aarch64
accumulate with one, so the polyfill emulates a correctly rounded fused
multiply-add (Boldo and Melquiond's algorithm, from Dekker's exact product and
Knuth's TwoSum). The emulation is exact unless a product or sum overflows or an
error term is subnormal. Those operands use the unfused expression. Rust's
`f64::round` rounds half away from zero exactly, while PHP 8.3's `round()`
first rounds to 15 significant digits. The polyfill therefore rounds through
its own exact function.

## Validation

Inputs are validated in the extension's order, so an input that is invalid in
several ways raises the same exception code.
